previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for a recurrent stage 4 sacral pressure ulcer and underwent successful sacral debridement with V-Y re-advancement flap coverage. He tolerated the procedure well, with stable postoperative course, adequate pain control, and gradual advancement to oral intake. He was transitioned from IV cefazolin to oral cefadroxil for antibiotic therapy. Despite fevers and a positive urine culture for Morganella morganii, he declined nephrostomy tube change during admission, though strongly advised to follow up with urology. He was discharged home with services, provided detailed wound and drain care instructions, and advised to use an air mattress and avoid pressure on the surgical site. Follow-up was arranged with plastic surgery, urology, and primary care, including imaging for a known lung nodule.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o male with a PMH of T12 paraplegia secondary to MVA
complicated by neurogenic bladder s/p ileal ___ and 
Left percutaneous nephrostomy tube for a ureteral stricture, 
presenting with fevers and flank pain and found to have a 
cellulitis and complicated cystitis treated with meropenem for 7 
days due to allergy and started on suppressive therapy with 
fosfomycin.

#Left nephrostomy site cellulitis and cystitis: patient 
presented with several weeks to months of puss draining from his 
nephrostomy site that had recently progressed to fevers, chills 
and left sided flank and back pain. Patient initially started on 
meropenem due to allergies and continued because of concern for 
GNR bacteremia. The blood culture was an error and deemed to be 
a GPR contaminant after several days. Patient was improving on 
meropenem and finished a 7 day course the day prior to 
discharge. He was started on suppressive fosfomycin therapy, and 
discharged after being observed off of antibiotics.

#Nausea and vomiting: On day two of hospitalization patient 
developed nausea and vomiting. Continued to eat, drink, and make 
stools daily and urine. Zofran offered multiple times, but 
patient declined. Improved off meropenem.

#Anemia: Patient had a hemoglobin of ~8 throughout his 
hospitalization which is stable near his baseline

#Anxiety: patient clearly anxious, has prescription for 
clonezepam 1mg TID at home that was continued after PMP checked.
